bullets.text: The essay argues that job-loss panic diverts attention from control over models, APIs, and compute.
It casts safety and geopolitical narratives as instruments for restricting access, rather than neutral warnings.
The business logic shifts from adding workers to lowering cost per outcome and raising revenue per employee.
The author acknowledges uneven gains and uncertainty about when broad productivity growth will support the workforce.
Individual reach does not equal structural power when compute, capital, and deployment remain concentrated.
The essay describes a feedback loop in which fear justifies regulation and regulation entrenches dominant providers.

sections.label: Human judgment and broken career ladders

bullets.text: The essay locates remaining human value in judgment while warning that productivity gains may concentrate pay.
Automation threatens the junior work that teaches expertise, without a corresponding reskilling safety net.
The proposed map distinguishes autonomous agents, solo AI-enabled operators, and people creating new economic categories.
The essay replaces employed-versus-unemployed framing with roles defined by how work is organized.
The doctor scenario shifts value from holding knowledge to coordinating people, models, and clinical decisions.
The closing centers discernment: knowing when to trust a model, override it, or ask a better question.

notes.text: The opening infers coordinated strategy from fundraising timing and policy relationships. What evidence would distinguish deliberate fear-based gatekeeping from genuinely held, if self-interested, concern about risk?

The section treats lean firms as evidence of leverage while acknowledging disappointing economy-wide gains. How far can a company's revenue per employee establish what AI will do for the wider workforce?
The argument prizes expert judgment yet says the routine work that trains experts is disappearing. How would new entrants develop the discernment on which the promised high-value roles depend?

In the doctor example, orchestration is more than delegating tasks. The distinctive human contribution is deciding when machine output deserves trust and when it should be overridden, so discernment remains necessary even as execution is redistributed.
